title: Marlow & Vane new-listing flyer batch: neutralize eight mixed-light property photos to an in-frame grey card, revive a washed-out lawn, vectorize the agency crest, and data-merge a listings roster into one press-ready flyer per property
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief ("We are seeking a talented designer to create a real estate flyer for a new listing. The flyer should be visually appealing and effectively communicate the property's features and benefits") and laundered to a fictional boutique agency, 'Marlow & Vane Realty' (agents Dana Marlow / Theo Vane) — no real company, person, agent, or trademark is named. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the raw brief implies a from-scratch flyer LAYOUT, which is NOT connector-doable (there is no free-form layout composition; document_merge_data_layout / document_render_layout only BIND/EXPORT a genuinely authored .indd, and a convert_pdf_to_indd template will not bind merge fields). So the agency is modeled as supplying a hand-authored single-record InDesign flyer template (.indd, one property per page) carrying live <<fields>> and TWO @-prefixed image-path columns (one for the property hero photo, one for the crest at the masthead), a listings roster CSV (one row per current new listing), eight raw agent-shot property photos each with a photographic 18% grey card laid in frame, and the flat agency crest as a scanned PNG on off-white stock. The Adobe chain does the genuinely-doable heavy lifting the brief rewards: neutralize every photo to its own in-frame grey card so the whole set shares one warm-editorial white point despite being shot under mismatched light, revive one overcast-flattened lawn to a natural green without a reshoot, prep-and-vectorize the scanned crest for razor-sharp print, then run the authored template through a one-file-per-row data-merge and export a press-ready PDF with one flyer per listing. 'New listing' is honored — the roster holds real per-listing fields (address, price, beds, baths, sqft, blurb, agent contact).
one_line_ask: Bring eight mixed-lighting property photos to one consistent, true-to-property look by neutralizing each to the 18% grey card it carries, decide per frame how far to move white balance without over-correcting, revive one washed-out front lawn to a natural green, prep and vectorize the agency crest, then data-merge the agency's authored single-record InDesign flyer template against the listings roster to produce one press-ready flyer per property.
full_brief: Marlow & Vane Realty, a boutique residential agency, needs its new-listing flyer sheet ready for print and the email blast — one clean US Letter portrait sheet per property, each carrying the listing's address, price, beds, baths, sqft and a short blurb alongside a strong hero photo, with the agency crest crisp at the top. We are NOT reshooting anything. We are handing you eight existing property photos and here is the problem: our agents shot them on different days under whatever light was there — some under flat cool overcast, a couple under warm tungsten room light, one kitchen under ugly fluorescent tubes, a couple of interiors underexposed against bright windows, one exterior blown out in midday sun — so straight out of the folder they look like a mismatched jumble, and a flyer set of mismatched shots reads cheap and amateur. To make this checkable we laid a photographic 18% grey card into a corner of every shot. Your job on the photos: bring every image to a consistent, welcoming, true-to-property look by neutralizing each one to the grey card it contains — the card must read as a clean neutral grey (equal across the channels) in your finished frame, and once every card is neutral the whole set will share one white point. Hold a subtle warm, inviting editorial feel in the final look (this is homes, not a burger ad — do not oversaturate), but do NOT force one blanket correction across the batch: each photo was lit differently and needs its own white-balance, exposure and tone decision to land on the shared target — warm the cool ones, cool the warm ones, recover the blown one, lift the dim ones. Be careful — at least one property is genuinely warm-toned (honey-oak floors, terracotta, low sun) and was shot under clean light, so its grey card already reads neutral; if you 'warm it to match the others' or chase an imagined blue cast you will strip the real character the buyer is being sold. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm the set is matched, not eyeballed. Second, one curb-appeal exterior was shot under dull overcast and the front lawn has gone a flat, tired khaki — bring the lawn back to a natural, healthy green (a believable revive in the SAME green family, just deepened and freshened — not radioactive turf, not a jump to a far-off color), and keep it to the lawn: the siding, sky, walkway and trim must stay exactly as graded, with the grass's own light and shadow intact. No flat dead-fill color, no whole-image tint that greens the whole photo. Third, our crest only exists as a flat scan on slightly off-white paper and it looks fuzzy at print size — get it clean and razor-sharp as a vector for the sheet masthead. Finally, build the sheets: we have hand-built the InDesign flyer template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the property hero photo, one for the crest at the top), and we are giving you the roster; merge them so every listing gets its own single-page flyer with its copy bound, its matching graded photo dropped into the hero frame, and the crisp crest dropped into the masthead, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF covering every listing (one page per property). Bind the copy verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite our addresses, prices or blurbs. Acceptance: every grey card neutral (channel spread within a hair of zero) and the whole set matched to one warm-editorial white point; the lawn revive natural and confined to the grass; the crest a crisp vector; and exactly one finished flyer per roster row.

inputs.name: listing_flyer_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US Letter (8.5x11) portrait new-listing flyer — ONE property per page, in a clean editorial style. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<address>>, <<price>>, <<beds>>, <<baths>>, <<sqft>>, <<blurb>>, <<agent_name>>, <<agent_phone>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a hero image frame (3:2) bound to @photo (the matching graded property photo), and a masthead crest frame at the top of the sheet bound to @crest (the vectorized agency crest). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the crest reaches the masthead ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind and paginate one page per roster row. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record flyer is the correct, connector-doable shape (a from-scratch or multi-up grid layout is out of connector scope). Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would NOT bind. TWO image columns (@photo, @crest) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's graded property photo AND the shared vectorized crest — so the chain-produced crest has a real, connector-doable path onto every flyer without any free-form placement (mirrors the AO-74 two-image-column pattern).

inputs.name: listings_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns address,price,beds,baths,sqft,blurb,agent_name,agent_phone,@photo,@crest holding EIGHT fictional current new listings for a boutique agency: a craftsman bungalow, a mid-century ranch, a downtown loft condo, a suburban colonial, a garden cottage, a lakeside a-frame, a townhouse, and a hillside contemporary. Realistic US addresses on FICTIONAL street names, list prices $415,000-$1,275,000, beds 1-4, baths 1-3.5, sqft 720-3,200, a one-line appetizing blurb per listing, and one of two fictional agents (Dana Marlow / Theo Vane) with fictional phone numbers. The @photo column names the matching prepped hero file (e.g. @capture_01_graded.jpg ... @capture_08_graded.jpg) so the [T] merge drops each graded photo into that row's hero frame. The @crest column holds the SAME vectorized crest file — @marlow_vane_crest.svg — in EVERY row, so the merge drops the one shared masthead mark onto every flyer as a merge bind (never free-form placement). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<address>>,<<price>>,<<beds>>,<<baths>>,<<sqft>>,<<blurb>>,<<agent_name>>,<<agent_phone>> and the two @image-path columns @photo and @crest. Do NOT include any column that names lighting, treatment, correction direction, or which frame is special — the roster describes listings only.
inputs.realism_notes: One row per new listing so the [T] data-merge paginates one flyer page per row; headers match the authored .indd merge fields exactly so binding succeeds. @crest carries the identical vectorized SVG path in all eight rows, giving the chain-produced crest a connector-doable path onto every flyer via the merge. Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight finished flyers. The @photo values are the agent's own neutral output filenames — the roster never encodes which capture was shot under which light, so it cannot telegraph the per-frame grade decision or which frame is the hold-WB trap.

inputs.name: raw_property_photos_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless camera captures of residential property, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera, roughly 4000x3000 or larger before crop), each with a photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, and each clearly visible and uncropped. Shot on different days under mismatched light, delivered under a NEUTRAL same-kind naming scheme (capture_01.jpg ... capture_08.jpg, all same extension) so nothing in the filename reveals the lighting or the correct treatment: (capture_01) craftsman bungalow front exterior on a flat cool OVERCAST afternoon, bluish cast, horizon tilted ~3 deg, the front lawn gone a dull tired khaki-green, a parked car partly at one edge; (capture_02) mid-century ranch exterior under near-neutral light but frame tilted ~4 deg; (capture_03) downtown loft living room under WARM TUNGSTEN room light, level; (capture_04) suburban colonial kitchen under ugly YELLOW-GREEN FLUORESCENT tubes giving an unpleasant cast, tilted ~3 deg, a dish rack at the counter edge; (capture_05) bungalow living room shot against a bright window so the interior sits UNDEREXPOSED and cool, level, a stray cable near the baseboard; (capture_06) ranch primary bedroom in DIM dusk light, underexposed and cool, level; (capture_07) a south-facing sunroom/living space with GENUINELY warm honey-oak floors and terracotta tile, shot under clean neutral daylight so its grey card already reads neutral (the warmth is the real material, not a white-balance error), level; (capture_08) loft rooftop exterior OVEREXPOSED in bright midday sun, blown highlights, warm, level. Every shot has real texture (siding, hardwood, tile, fabric), candid documentary real-estate feel, cluttered edges, no HDR gloss, no virtual staging, no CGI. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA capture at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each 3:2 hero crop can fill the flyer hero frame at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Deliberately mismatched (per-frame WB, exposure and tilt vary; only frames 01/02/04 are tilted) so a single blanket correction cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own decision, and the directions OPPOSE (warm the cool frames 01/05/06, cool the warm frames 03/08, neutralize+de-green the fluorescent frame 04, small nudge on near-neutral frame 02). The in-frame 18% grey card is the free, checkable neutral target. TRAP FRAME: capture_07's warmth is real material color under clean light and its card already reads neutral — a naive agent that batch-applies the same 'warm it to match' move used on the cool frames (or cools an imagined cast) will neutralize its card OFF-neutral and strip the honey/terracotta character; the correct move is to HOLD white balance and only match brightness. capture_01 additionally carries the washed-out lawn for the masked green revive. Edge clutter (parked car, dish rack, cable) is handled by CROPPING to the hero frame, never by object removal/inpainting. The neutral capture_0N naming and the grey card mean the agent must OPEN each frame to decide its treatment — the filename never reveals it.

inputs.name: marlow_vane_crest_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Marlow & Vane Realty' monogram crest inked on slightly off-white textured paper: a refined serif 'M&V' inside a thin-line shield outline with 'MARLOW & VANE REALTY' set beneath, deep dark-navy ink. Rendered as a scan — the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly (solid navy, no gradients).
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, crisp/drop the off-white ground, crop to the mark, knock the paper to transparency, THEN vectorize. Solid dark-navy with no gradients so the trace is clean. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible crest lettering. Filename names the goal (a crest to vectorize), not a treatment trap.

outputs.name: MarlowVane_Listing_Flyers_print.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready US Letter (8.5x11) portrait new-listing flyers — ONE single-record flyer per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each flyer binds its address/price/beds/baths/sqft/blurb/agent_name/agent_phone verbatim from the roster with its matching grey-card-neutralized 3:2 photo dropped into the hero frame (via @photo) and the vectorized crest dropped into the masthead frame (via @crest) — both by merge bind, never free-form placement; ~300 DPI print quality. A 'hero' listing is simply the first page of this merged PDF — no per-record file is exported separately.

outputs.name: graded_property_photos_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-neutralized, straightened property photos, delivered as the hero-framed 3:2 crops (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralized masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on the RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master of each frame (the *_neutralized output, its in-frame 18% grey card still present) — the card region reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared warm-editorial white point, and true-to-property (no frame's genuine character forced off — capture_07's warmth held); (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered hero-framed 3:2 crop (the *_graded output that binds into that listing's flyer) — it is framed on the property with the grey card fully cropped OUT (no card pixels present). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed hero crop. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame.

outputs.name: variant_hero_lawn_revived.jpg
outputs.spec: The capture_01 curb-appeal hero with its washed-out front lawn revived to a natural, healthy green via a masked, luminosity-preserving image_adjust_hsl pass on the grass only (a small within-family green-band hue/saturation lift that deepens and freshens the tired khaki, an in-band adjacent shift — no near-complementary rotation), riding the grass's existing luminosity so its blade texture, light and shadow stay natural; the siding, sky, walkway and trim stay exactly as graded — no whole-image overlay, no flat fill. This is the graded+lawn-revived version that binds into the craftsman-bungalow flyer.

outputs.name: marlow_vane_crest.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the Marlow & Vane monogram crest, traced only after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark, and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground or skew.

connector_workflow.note: Prep-before-trace step 1: the crest scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drop the off-white paper toward white so the navy mark separates hard from the ground — a soft, low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges. Single primitive-built adjustments call.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the crest, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms and shield only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill).

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids.
Triage: this curb-appeal exterior is tilted ~3 deg — level it first. (Only the tilted frames 01/02/04 get straightened; the level frames skip this — deciding which is part of the job.)

Cool overcast cast: WARM it (positive temperature) and set tint until the in-frame 18% grey card reads neutral (R=G=B), then set exposure/highlights/shadows so the card sits at mid-grey and hold the subtle warm-editorial house tone with a touch of vibrance/clarity. Reason the exact temperature/exposure to THIS card — do not reuse another frame's numbers. Report the final move. (Replaces the deprecated color_temperature / dark_portions / vibrance_and_saturation with one image_apply_adjustments call.)

On the graded full-res curb-appeal frame, semantically select only the front lawn ('the front lawn grass in front of the house'). Isolates the revive to the grass so the siding, sky, walkway and trim are untouched. Returns a maskURI. Not a hue/coordinate selection — a real named object.

Masked revive (consumes frame + lawn mask): keep the grass in the green family but deepen and freshen the tired khaki — a small within-band green-band hue nudge plus a saturation lift and a slight luminance settle, letting the grass's existing luminosity carry the blade texture and shadow. Confined to the mask. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would green the whole photo) and image_fill_area is flat solid dead-fill (kills the grass texture) — both are wrong here. A moderate adjacent-hue move, never a near-complementary rotation.

Crop the neutralized+lawn-revived frame to the 3:2 hero the flyer expects, framing on the house with the grey card and the edge-parked car cropped OUT — this hero crop (card removed) binds into the bungalow flyer via @photo. The pre-crop neutralized master (cap01_neutralized, grey card in frame) is RETAINED by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifact; the card's neutrality is graded THERE, never on this crop. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never generative-expand.
Tilted ~4 deg — level it.

Near-neutral light: its grey card is close to neutral, so only a SMALL white-balance nudge is needed to land on the shared white point — over-correcting would push it off the set. Set exposure to match set brightness, hold the warm-editorial tone. Report the (small) move.
Crop to the 3:2 hero frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Warm tungsten room light, level frame: this frame must move the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames — COOL it (negative temperature) until its grey card reads neutral and it matches the shared white point. Adaptive: the batch is not uniformly cool, so a blanket 'warm everything' pass fails here. Report the move.
Crop to the 3:2 hero frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.
Tilted ~3 deg under fluorescent light — level it.

Ugly yellow-green fluorescent cast: correct white balance toward neutral daylight against the grey card and set exposure to the set brightness — but a temperature/tint move alone leaves a lingering green tinge fluorescent tubes are notorious for. Report the move; the green residue is handled next.

Knock down the lingering fluorescent green: a green-band saturation reduction (and slight luminance settle) so the cabinets/counters read true and the card finishes clean neutral — the tint slider alone can't fully kill a fluorescent green residue, so this second HSL beat is the reasoned fix. Keep it to the green band; do not desaturate the whole frame.
Crop to the 3:2 hero frame, trimming the cluttered dish-rack counter edge and the grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Backlit window, underexposed cool interior: LIFT exposure and shadows to recover the dim room, THEN warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point — the dominant move here is tonal AND WB, protect the window highlights from clipping. Report the move.
Crop to the 3:2 hero frame, trimming the stray baseboard cable and the grey card OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Dim dusk, underexposed cool bedroom: lift exposure and gently open shadows so the room is welcoming, then warm to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point. Different starting point from frame 05 (dusk vs window backlight) so distinct numbers. Report the move.
Crop to the 3:2 hero frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

THE TRAP FRAME. The honey-oak/terracotta space is genuinely warm and it was shot under clean neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set and hold a touch of the house tone). A naive agent that batch-applies the same 'warm the cool cast' move used on frames 01/05/06, or that 'cools an imagined cast', will neutralize the card off-neutral and strip the real warm character the buyer is being sold. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was held.
Crop to the 3:2 hero frame, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Overexposed warm midday exterior: PULL exposure/highlights DOWN to recover the blown roofline, then COOL to neutralize its grey card to the shared white point. Opposite tonal AND WB direction from the underexposed frames 05/06 — proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. Report the move.
Crop to the 3:2 hero frame, grey card cropped OUT. Frames 01-08 now share one warm-editorial white point, each neutralized to its own grey card. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: capture_01_graded, capture_02_graded, capture_03_graded, capture_04_graded, capture_05_graded, capture_06_graded, capture_07_graded, capture_08_graded, marlow_vane_crest.svg
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the eight grey-card-neutralized 3:2 hero crops plus the vector crest so the merge can resolve them by the @photo column (per-row hero) and the @crest column (the shared masthead mark). Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references (e.g. marlow_vane_crest.svg for @crest).

Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @photo and @crest columns resolve to — the per-listing graded photo and the shared vectorized crest — for each single-record flyer's hero frame and masthead frame.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (address/price/beds/baths/sqft/blurb/agent_name/agent_phone) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve BOTH image columns per row — drop that row's graded hero photo into the @photo frame AND the vectorized crest (from @crest, the same SVG in every row) into the masthead frame — producing EXACTLY ONE merged flyer per row (eight flyers). Binding the crest through the @crest image column is what puts it on the masthead: free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, so the merge is its only connector-doable path. [T] requires the hand-authored template with its two merge-wired image frames. A multi-record grid or a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind — neither is used.

Export the merged single-record flyers to a press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF, one flyer per listing. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all eight flyers, one page per property) in a single call — it cannot export one named record on its own, so a 'hero' listing is simply the first page of this set, not a separate file. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. The crest runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain: straighten(1) -> crisp adjustments(2) -> crop_to_bounds(3) -> remove_background to transparency(4) -> vectorize(5). Eight per-photo grade sub-chains fan out from the raw zip, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralization (adaptive per frame: warm the cool frames 01/05/06, cool the warm frames 03/08, neutralize+de-green the fluorescent frame 04 across TWO beats, small nudge on near-neutral frame 02, recover the overexposed frame 08, and HOLD white balance on the genuinely-warm trap frame 07) followed by a 3:2 hero crop, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames 01/02/04 — every neutralization driven to that frame's own in-frame grey card so all eight converge on one shared warm-editorial white point. The curb-appeal frame (cap01_neutralized, step 7) additionally feeds the masked lawn revive: image_select_by_prompt(8) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(9) -> hero crop(10); the fluorescent frame runs a two-beat correction: WB image_apply_adjustments(17) -> green-band image_adjust_hsl(18) -> crop(19). The eight graded hero crops and the crest SVG converge into the upload session(28) -> finalize(29) -> document_merge_data_layout(30), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and emits one merged flyer per row, resolving BOTH the @photo column (that row's graded hero) and the @crest column (the shared vectorized crest, identical in every row) into the template's two merge-wired image frames — the only connector-doable path for the crest since free-form placement is banned. The merged set is exported once, by document_render_layout(31), to the single press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF carrying all eight flyers (one page per property); no per-record named export is attempted. Nothing after the raw loads originates outside the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 31 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/vectorize, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 upload steps and the 3 auto_straighten auto-ops. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the eight neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (cool frames warmed, warm frames cooled, one underexposed frame lifted, one overexposed frame recovered, a fluorescent frame neutralized then de-greened, one genuinely-warm frame HELD) all forced to converge on a single measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — so a blanket batch correction cannot pass. Layered on top are a masked, luminosity-preserving lawn revive (a within-family khaki->healthy-green deepen the masked image_adjust_hsl path can actually hold — no near-complementary rotation, with a written rationale for why color_overlay and fill_area are both wrong), a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white crest scan, and a two-image-column one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template (the row's graded hero via @photo and the shared vectorized crest via @crest, so the crest reaches the masthead as a merge bind rather than banned free-form placement). Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling, no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (the template is a supplied authored .indd); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; edge clutter (car, dish rack, cable) is handled by CROPPING; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _dark_portions / _vibrance_and_saturation / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): every photo carries a physical 18% grey card in frame and the acceptance criterion is that each frame's card, graded on its RETAINED pre-crop neutralized master (the *_neutralized full-res frame the harness keeps, card still present), reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a hair of zero) with the whole set matched to one warm-editorial white point — a target the agent can miss, and it must REPORT the final white-balance and exposure move per frame so 'matched' is verifiable rather than asserted; card-exclusion is a SEPARATE gate checked on the hero-framed 3:2 crops (the *_graded outputs, card cropped OUT) that bind into the flyers, so the neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-removed hero crop; the merge adds a third checkable gate (output page-count must equal roster row-count = 8, since document_merge_data_layout is one-file-per-row). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset neutralization of eight differently-lit property shots to a common measurable white point, each needing its own opposite-direction correction (warm/cool/lift/recover/de-green); (2) a masked, luminosity-preserving khaki->healthy-green lawn revive (a within-family adjacent shift image_adjust_hsl can reliably hold, not a near-complementary rotation) that must keep the grass texture and shadow natural and touch nothing else, using the only masked recolor path (image_adjust_hsl), not color_overlay (whole-image) or fill_area (flat dead-fill); (3) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed, off-white, margin-padded crest scan (straighten->crisp->crop-to-bounds->knock-to-transparency) before vectorize.
